title: Mid-Term Tier Upgrades on Homeowner Service Contracts
content:
**Eligibility.** A Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts tier may be upgraded mid-term only when the current tier's mid-term upgrade setting is Yes and the contract status is waiting period or active. Both are read from the contract record before the upgrade.

**What an upgrade is.** An upgrade moves to any higher-ranked tier; a move to a lower-ranked tier is a downgrade and is processed only at renewal under the renewal terms. Tier rank runs from Bridgewell ApplianceCare (lowest) through Bridgewell SystemsCare, Bridgewell HomeCare Bronze, Bridgewell HomeCare Silver and Bridgewell HomeCare Gold to Bridgewell HomeCare Platinum (highest).

**Effect.** The upgrade takes effect on the date the customer requests it, records the tier held before it as the prior tier, and keeps the current term dates.

**Billing.**
- *Monthly-billed contract:* installments for billing periods starting on or after the upgrade date are billed at the new tier's monthly installment, and no proration is billed.
- *Annual-billed contract:* one upgrade proration charge is billed on the upgrade date, equal to the new tier's annual premium minus the current tier's annual premium (each computed for this contract under the premium pricing rule), multiplied by the unexpired term days and divided by the term days, rounded to the cent. For this purpose the two day counts are taken as of the upgrade date: the unexpired term days are the calendar days from the day after the upgrade date through the term end date inclusive (zero when the upgrade date is on or after the term end date), and the term days are the calendar days from the term start date through the term end date inclusive.

When to cover items and higher limits added by an upgrade is governed by the coverage determination rules.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).** An annual-billed contract whose current annual premium is 600.00 and whose new tier's annual premium for the same contract is 700.00; the term runs 365 days and 146 days remain after the upgrade date. The difference is 100.00; multiplied by 146 and divided by 365 this gives 40.00, the proration charge.

| Situation | Upgrade allowed? |
|---|---|
| Tier setting Yes, contract active | Yes |
| Tier setting Yes, contract in its waiting period | Yes |
| Tier setting Yes, contract suspended for nonpayment | No |
| Tier setting No (Bridgewell HomeCare Platinum) | No |
